chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and he said: Wash your right hand from the elbow to your fingers, and urinate if you are able to urinate. Then put your hand into the vessel, then wash whatever of it has touched you. Then pour water over your head and body, and there is no wudu (ablution) in it.

key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: the vessel containing the water used for washing
key_terms.الْيُمْنَى: the right hand, specified as the first limb to wash
key_terms.تَغْسِلُ: you wash; an instruction for the procedure
key_terms.جَسَدِكَ: your body, which is included in the ghusl washing
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, over which water is to be poured in ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath performed after the state of janabah
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), which the hadith says is not separately required here

ai.seo_question: What is the method of ghusl al-janabah according to Imam al-Rida عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah and describes its order. It indicates washing the right hand first, urinating if able, then washing and pouring water over the head and body, and it states that no separate wudu (ablution) is required within it.
